title: Graph Journey
description: DFS/BFS, connectivity, union-find, topological order, shortest paths, spanning trees, and Euler trails.

prerequisites: Heap basics before weighted shortest paths
journey.outcome: Model vertices and edges explicitly, then select traversal, ordering, connectivity, or weighted-path algorithms by their assumptions.

connections.number-of-islands: Begin with an implicit grid graph and flood-fill one component at a time. Mark cells when discovered so a neighbor cannot enqueue or recurse into the same work repeatedly.
connections.max-area-of-island: Reuse flood fill while returning a component aggregate. Count cells in the current component separately from the maximum across all components.
connections.clone-graph: Separate original vertex identity from copied vertex identity. Create and memoize a clone before following its neighbors, so cycles and shared neighbors do not create duplicate copies.
connections.number-of-connected-components-in-an-und: Move from a grid to an adjacency-list graph. Start a traversal from every unvisited vertex, including isolated vertices with no incident edges.
connections.graph-valid-tree: Connectivity alone is insufficient for a tree. Combine reaching every vertex with absence of cycles, or use the connected graph's required edge count.
connections.is-graph-bipartite: Carry a color constraint across edges instead of only visited state. Every component must be checked, and an edge joining equal colors is a contradiction.
connections.redundant-connection: Replace repeated reachability searches with disjoint-set union. An edge whose endpoints already share a representative is exactly the one that closes a cycle.
connections.accounts-merge: Use the same union-find machinery with a domain-specific identity relation. Shared email addresses join records, while equal display names alone do not prove the same account.
connections.course-schedule: Switch to a directed dependency graph. Undirected parent-skipping no longer detects cycles correctly; use recursion-stack colors or an indegree-zero processing queue.
connections.course-schedule-ii: Retain the order from indegree removal instead of only checking feasibility. A partial ordering that omits a cycle is not a valid schedule for all courses.
connections.alien-dictionary: Construct the dependency graph from observations rather than receiving edges directly. Only the first differing character of adjacent words creates an edge; invalid prefix order is a separate failure case.
connections.rotting-oranges: Use BFS layers as elapsed time and initialize the frontier with every source. Reaching a cell first gives its earliest arrival when every edge takes one unit.
connections.walls-and-gates: Reuse multi-source BFS to fill a whole distance field. Starting from every gate avoids solving an independent shortest-path search for each room.
connections.word-ladder: Generate an unweighted graph's neighbors on demand from word edits. BFS still gives shortest distance; the main design choice is efficient valid-neighbor generation.
connections.dijkstras-algorithm: Replace FIFO layers with a minimum-distance heap when nonnegative edge weights differ. Ignore stale heap entries and relax only genuine improvements.
connections.network-delay-time: Apply the same weighted shortest-path solver to a directed network. The final broadcast time is the largest reachable shortest distance, and one unreachable node makes the broadcast incomplete.
connections.bellman-ford: Remove Dijkstra's nonnegative-edge assumption. Repeated edge relaxation handles negative weights, while an extra improvement pass exposes a negative cycle reachable from the source.
connections.cheapest-flights-within-k-stops: Add an edge-count budget to relaxation. A cheaper route using too many edges cannot replace every more expensive route; copied distance layers preserve the allowed number of flights.
connections.floyd-warshall: Move from one source to all pairs on a small graph. The DP state permits an increasing set of intermediate vertices, so the intermediate-vertex loop must be outermost.
connections.prims-algorithm: Change the objective from one source's shortest routes to connecting all vertices with minimum total edge cost. Prim grows one component; Kruskal combines sorted edges with the union-find pattern learned earlier.
connections.min-cost-to-connect-all-points: Apply the spanning-tree objective when edge costs are derived from coordinates. Manhattan distance defines a complete graph, which can be handled without confusing it with shortest-path distance from one point.
connections.swim-in-rising-water: Interview stretch: a route's cost is its maximum elevation rather than the sum of weights. Re-derive relaxation with max, or view rising water as a monotonic connectivity threshold.
connections.reconstruct-itinerary: Interview stretch: use every edge once rather than merely visiting vertices. Repeated tickets are distinct edges, and an Euler-trail construction must preserve the required lexical order.

topics.name: Traversal and graph modeling
topics.description: Identify components, aggregate reachable nodes, and preserve identity while traversing cycles.

topics.name: Disjoint-set connectivity
topics.description: Use representatives, path compression, and balanced unions to maintain changing components.

topics.name: Directed cycles and topological order
topics.description: Distinguish dependencies from undirected connectivity and construct only justified ordering edges.

topics.name: Unweighted shortest paths
topics.description: Use BFS layers, multiple starting points, and implicit neighbors to compute earliest arrivals.

topics.name: Weighted shortest-path families
topics.description: Choose algorithms by edge signs, source count, and path-length constraints rather than by habit.

topics.name: Spanning trees and graph extensions
topics.description: Separate total connectivity cost, bottleneck paths, and trails that must consume every edge.
